reason: The cited evidence supports feasibility, hardness, and wear resistance of similar HEA coatings, but provides no direct support for high-temperature performance up to 800 °C, corrosion resistance in aggressive media, or the specific protective oxide mechanism on 316L.
premises: Laser cladding of FeCoNiCrMo0.2-based HEA coatings on 316L stainless steel is feasible and yields a refined, metallurgically bonded microstructure.
The HEA coating enhances surface hardness and wear resistance relative to uncoated 316L.
The HEA coating improves corrosion resistance in aggressive media (e.g., seawater).
The coating remains effective under elevated temperatures up to ~800 °C.
The improvements are mediated by solid-solution strengthening and protective oxide formation.
